It elaborates biological aging mechanisms and central sensitization, gives psychological therapies a central role, and adds social access/care-system factors. synthesis_note: This review contributes a qualitative synthesis of determinants of PNE acceptance, showing substantive BPS content: biological pain mechanisms, psychological beliefs/affect/trust, and social/organizational relationships/culture. It offers several cross-domain pathways, especially biomedical beliefs, group support, clinician trust, and professional culture. It does not provide a full reciprocal BPS model; mechanisms remain tentative and implementation-focused.

synthesis_note: The review contributes a prognostic inventory of chronic postsurgical pain risk factors after hip replacement, with substantive biological and psychological constructs and sparse socioeconomic evidence. It uses biopsychosocial language and combines risk factors, but does not specify how biological, psychological, and social domains interact. Social content is mostly inferred from general chronic pain literature rather than THA data.
coding_rationale: BPS is used as a prognostic risk-factor frame: biological and psychological factors dominate, social evidence is sparse. Triadic integration is partial; no three-domain mechanism is proposed.

synthesis_note: The review operationalizes BPS mainly as self-management for TMD: psychological interventions (education, behavioural therapy, CBT) plus jaw exercises and pain/function outcomes. It names patient-centred/patient-perspective and provider roles but does not analyse social determinants or relationships. It offers one bio-psy behavioural route and a psychosocial correlation, not a three-domain mechanism.
coding_rationale: Social content is thin but present; it does not enter the mechanism. Bio-psy integration is mechanistic via behavioural jaw-system work, and psychosocial function is described as correlating with TMD course.

synthesis_note: It contributes a TGD-youth narrative synthesis that operationalizes BPS as neurobiological vulnerability, psychosocial distress/minority stress, and social/systemic barriers. Its strongest contribution is a triadic mechanism linking stigma and chronic stress to HPA-axis, inflammatory/sensitization pathways and pain. It does not test this model with primary data, and many proposed mechanisms remain under-evidenced.
coding_rationale: All three domains are substantive. Mechanistic triadic integration is supported by the minority-stress/HPA-axis/inflammation/sensitization pathway. Close call: GAHT claims are partly theoretical and evidence is narrative.

synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS largely by shifting attention to the social domain. It elaborates eight social dimensions and links them to chronic pain through stress, isolation, stigma, work/living conditions, and lifestyle. Biological content is incidental and psychological content is secondary. It does not provide a three-domain mechanism or show how biomedical, psychological, and social factors interact as a system.
coding_rationale: Social domain dominates; bio is only incidental and psych secondary. Pairwise social-bio and social-psych pathways are proposed, but no triadic mechanism; pseudo_bps reflects thin/parallel bio-psy treatment.

synthesis_note: This state-of-the-art review translates psychosocial care into orthopaedic practice. It treats psychological constructs, assessment, interventions and implementation as central, and gives substantial attention to social/system/cultural determinants. Biological factors are present mainly as pain, surgery, rehabilitation and recovery outcomes. It offers descriptive triadic BPS links but no explicit cross-domain mechanism.
coding_rationale: Psychosocial content and social implementation barriers dominate; biology is contextual. All three domains are related descriptively, but no pathway is specified. Resilience definition and psychosocial measurement heterogeneity are key close calls.

synthesis_note: This postpartum-recovery review operationalizes BPS mainly through ICF domains and risk-factor categories. Biological and psychological factors dominate; social content is present but thin and no social-participation outcomes were found. It proposes a descriptive triadic account and some directional associations, but no cross-domain mechanism.
coding_rationale: ICF/BPS organize domains; physical and mental domains dominate. Social participation is absent and social support thin. Triadic integration is descriptive, not mechanistic.

synthesis_note: It offers an integrative review of chronic non-cancer pain using Whittemore and Knafl, extracting 44 studies across biological, psychosocial, social/gender, and cultural determinants. It argues for reciprocal biopsychosocial interaction, including fear-avoidance and social support/strain. It does not fully specify detailed mediators or operational definitions, and longitudinal/intervention evidence remains limited.
coding_rationale: All three domains are substantive, but social evidence is underexplored. Integration is mechanistic at triadic level due to reciprocal interaction claims, though detailed pathways are broad. Close call: cultural factors extend beyond BPS.

It links domains through pain modulation enabling movement, expectations shaped by family/culture/health system, fear-avoidance/deconditioning, therapeutic alliance, and Pain-Movement Interface feedback loops. synthesis_note: The paper operationalizes BPS mainly as a rationale for composite outcomes in implantable neuromodulation for refractory pain. It names physical, mental and social domains and many measures, but does not model how domains interact or change together. Its contribution is measurement-focused and descriptive rather than mechanistic.
coding_rationale: All domains are present but largely listed as outcome dimensions. Triadic integration is descriptive only; no pathway is proposed. The BPS label supports a composite-outcome argument, not a true integrative model.

synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS for TGD youth by expanding it with minority stress, ecological-systems, and intersectional models. It offers substantive cross-domain mechanisms linking structural inequity, distress/coping, and pain-system dysregulation, while emphasizing resilience and gender affirmation. It does not fill all evidence gaps: TGD youth remain underrepresented, some associations lack causal pathways, and assessment tools are often mismatched.
coding_rationale: All three domains are elaborated and repeatedly linked through stress, coping, and pain-system pathways. Triadic integration is mechanistic via ecological/systems reasoning. Social framing is dominant because gender diversity and structural inequity organize the review.

synthesis_note: The review maps existential therapies for chronic pain and shows that existential/psychological constructs—meaningfulness, death anxiety, acceptance, identity, spirituality, anxiety/depression, self-efficacy—are commonly used and often reported as improved. integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes that nociplastic pain is maintained by central sensitization/neuroplasticity and a hyperactive salience/alarm system. Fear, catastrophizing, avoidance, and misinterpretation of harmless signals amplify the alarm; education, exposure, cognitive restructuring, emotional processing, and neuroplastic relearning calm the system and reduce pain. synthesis_note: The review operationalizes BPS mainly as neurocognitive impairment within chronic pain and XR rehabilitation. Biological/neurophysiological and psychological mechanisms are developed, especially pain–cognition and XR-mediated attention/emotion/memory pathways. Social content is mainly healthcare implementation and patient/stakeholder barriers. It does not provide a genuine three-domain mechanism.
coding_rationale: Bio and psych are substantive and mechanistically linked; social is mainly implementation context. Triadic integration is partial rather than descriptive/mechanistic; BPS language is not analytically integrated.

While substantive content is developed for biological and psychological domains, social factors are mentioned but less elaborated. The integration is descriptive rather than mechanistic, representing a multifactorial rather than truly integrative BPS approach. integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes multiple mechanistic pathways linking pain and stress across biological, psychological, and social domains. Biological mechanisms include HPA axis activation, neurotransmitter imbalances (dopamine, serotonin), neuroinflammation, and central sensitization. Psychological mechanisms involve catastrophizing, fear-avoidance, and hypervigilance, which alter brain connectivity and stress responses. Social mechanisms include socioeconomic stress, social support buffering, and interpersonal dynamics affecting pain perception. These pathways create bidirectional reinforcement loops, particularly through stress activating biological changes that perpetuate pain, and pain creating social stress that exacerbates the cycle.
